source.title: Some Open Problems in Matrix Theory Arising in Linear Systems and Control

accepted.question_text: Given a collection M of real n x n matrices, determine a subset M_0 subseteq M with the property that if every matrix in M_0 is stable, meaning that all of its eigenvalues have negative real part, then every matrix in M is stable. The source highlights this as a fundamental robust-stability problem for uncertain linear-system models and asks for such certifying subsets beyond the polynomial cases covered by Kharitonov-type results.
accepted.context_brief: robust stability certification by a test subset

evidence.quote: A fundamental problem in the analysis of linear systems is the following: Given a collection of matrices M c R^{n x n}, determine a subset M_0 c M such that if every element of M_0 is stable (that is, each of its eigenvalues has negative real part), then every element of M is also stable.
This problem arises when the modeling data are uncertain and guarantees of stability are desired.

accepted.question_text: For the interval family of companion-form matrices displayed in equations (2.6)-(2.7), find a direct proof using only matrix-theoretic arguments that checking the four matrices in M_0 suffices to guarantee stability of the whole family. The source explains that the known proof is only an immediate consequence of Kharitonov's polynomial theorem, and it asks for a genuinely matrix-based proof that could lead to stronger results for more general matrix polytopes.
accepted.context_brief: matrix-based proof of a Kharitonov-type four-matrix test

evidence.quote: That M_0 given by (2.7) is sufficient is an immediate consequence of Kharitonov's result, since each matrix is in companion form.
A direct, matrix-based proof of this result is unknown. Such a proof could lead to improvements in treating more general matrix polytopes.

accepted.question_text: Let A and B be square matrices with algebraic entries. If exp(A) exp(B) = exp(A + B), must A and B commute? The source notes that commutativity is known under the stronger hypothesis exp(A) exp(B) = exp(B) exp(A) for algebraic matrices, but states that the case exp(A) exp(B) = exp(A + B) remains open.

evidence.quote: If however, A and A have only algebraic entries then e^A e^A = e^A e^A implies that A and A commute [85, 86].
If A and A have algebraic entries and e^A e^A = e^{A+A}, then it is reasonable to conjecture that A and A must commute, but this case is not discussed in [85] and remains open.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a nonnormal matrix A such that either exp(A) exp(A^T) = exp(A^T) exp(A) or exp(A) exp(A^T) = exp(A + A^T)? The question asks whether a nonnormal real matrix can satisfy either of these exponential identities involving its transpose.
accepted.context_brief: transpose-related exponential identities for nonnormal matrices

evidence.quote: Specializing to the case A = A^T, a related open question is the following [14]: Does there exist a nonnormal matrix A satisfying either e^A e^{A^T} = e^{A^T} e^A or e^A e^{A^T} = e^{A+A^T}?

accepted.question_text: Can the spectral inequalities tr(exp(A + B)) <= tr(exp(A)exp(B)), tr(exp(A)exp(A^T)) <= tr(exp(A + A^T)), and lambda_max(exp(A)exp(A^T)) <= lambda_max(exp(A + A^T)) be derived directly from one of the matrix-exponential formulas (3.8), (3.9), or (3.10)? The source identifies this as an open route for explaining inequalities (3.13)-(3.15) from structural exponential expansions.
accepted.context_brief: deriving exponential inequalities from expansion formulas

evidence.quote: An interesting open question that immediately arises is whether or not it is possible to derive (3.12)-(3.15) directly from any of the formulas (3.8), (3.9) or (3.10).
In this regard (3.10) appears to be the most promising candidate.

accepted.question_text: Find a useful generalization of the inequality tr(exp(A)exp(A^T)) <= tr(exp(A + A^T)) that remains informative for large time in stability problems by incorporating a Lyapunov weighting term of the form exp(A^T P + P A), where P is positive definite and chosen so that A^T P + P A is negative definite. The source proposes this as a way to avoid the conservatism of the naive bound as t tends to infinity.

evidence.quote: Hence if A is stable, then the left-hand side of (3.16) will converge to zero, whereas the right-hand side may be unbounded, rendering the bound useless.

To resolve the possible conservatism in (3.16) for t -> infinity, it is natural to conjecture generalizations of (3.14) to include terms of the form e^{A^T P + P A}, where the positive definite matrix P is chosen as in Lyapunov stability theory to render A^T P + P A negative definite.

accepted.question_text: Do there exist normed spaces D and E for which the H_2 norm of a linear-system transfer function is an induced operator norm? The source asks whether one can realize the H_2 performance measure as a true induced norm between suitable signal spaces rather than only as an energy-like quantity.
accepted.context_brief: whether the H2 norm is induced

evidence.quote: Immediately this raises the following question: Do there exist normed spaces D and E such that the H_2 norm is induced?
Hence, by (4.7), J = ||G(s)||_2^2, where || . ||_2 denotes the H_2 norm [31].

accepted.question_text: Is the Frobenius norm on the space of m x n real matrices an induced matrix norm if one is allowed to place different norms on the domain R^n and codomain R^m? The source explains that it is not induced when the same norm is used on both spaces, but leaves open whether asymmetric choices of vector norms could induce the Frobenius norm.
accepted.context_brief: inducedness of the Frobenius matrix norm

evidence.quote: From (4.7) the answer to this question would appear to be related to the following question: Is the Frobenius matrix norm induced?

Since ||I_n||_F = sqrt(n), the answer is no if the domain and range spaces of I_n are assigned the same norms. However, this does not rule out the possibility of assigning different norms to, say R^m and R^n for inducing the Frobenius norm of M in R^{m x n}. This remains a fundamental open problem.

accepted.question_text: For matrix norms that satisfy submultiplicativity or mixed submultiplicativity, determine whether such norms must be induced norms or whether some of them cannot be induced. The source explicitly asks for a structural characterization of inducedness within these broader multiplicative classes.

evidence.quote: More generally, it is possible to define matrix norms that satisfy submultiplicativity ... or mixed submultiplicativity ... conditions [37-39].
Is it possible to show that such norms are induced or cannot be induced?

accepted.question_text: Given matrices A, B, and C defining the linear system x'(t) = A x(t) + B u(t), y(t) = C x(t), determine necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a static output-feedback matrix K such that A + B K C is asymptotically stable. This is the classic output-feedback stabilizability problem for systems without full-state access.

evidence.quote: One of the most basic unsolved problems in control theory is the problem of output feedback stabilizability: Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on (A, B, C) under which there exists K such that A + BKC is asymptotically stable.
Conditions for exact stabilizability, however, are unknown.

accepted.question_text: For the decentralized static controller with block-diagonal gains u_i(t) = K_i y_i(t) across r feedback channels, determine when there exist gains K_1, ..., K_r such that the closed-loop matrix A + sum_i B_i K_i C_i is stable. The source frames this as the decentralized analogue of centralized output-feedback stabilization and states that the available theory is incomplete.

evidence.quote: For this problem the objective is to determine whether K_1, ..., K_r exist such that the closed-loop dynamics matrix A + sum_i B_i K_i C_i is stable.
Although some results have been obtained for this problem [3], the theory is far from complete.

accepted.question_text: Given a dynamic compensator of prescribed order n_c < n for the system x'(t) = A x(t) + B u(t), y(t) = C x(t), determine necessary and sufficient conditions under which there exist controller matrices A_c, B_c, and C_c of that reduced order that stabilize the closed loop. The source notes that the full-order case n_c = n is understood, whereas the reduced-order case remains unsolved.

evidence.quote: If n_c = n, then necessary and sufficient conditions for stabilizability are well known, namely, (A, B) must be stabilizable and (C, A) must be detectable [53].
Stabilizability for the case n_c < n is unsolved; for partial results see [59, 73].

accepted.question_text: Characterize, and ideally parameterize, the full set of feedback gains that stabilize a given linear system under the output-feedback structures discussed in the source. Such a parameterization should make it possible to optimize additional design criteria once stabilization is achieved.

evidence.quote: Beyond the question of existence, it is of interest to be able to characterize (and perhaps parameterize) the set of stabilizing feedback gains.
Such a parameterization would then be useful for selecting gains with desirable properties beyond stabilization.

accepted.question_text: For output feedback, determine when one can assign the closed-loop poles to a prescribed region or to prescribed locations in the left half-plane by choosing suitable feedback gains. The source emphasizes that, unlike the full-state-feedback case, output-feedback pole placement is still essentially unsolved even though partial results are known.

evidence.quote: A refinement of the stabilizability problem is the pole (i.e., eigenvalue) assignability problem. In this problem the goal is to determine feedback gains that place the closed-loop spectrum within a specified region or at specified locations in the left half plane.

In the output-feedback case, however, controllability and pole placement are not equivalent. Although this problem is essentially unsolved, some partial results are available [1, 17, 26, 30, 45, 49, 71, 78].

accepted.question_text: Understand the existence, uniqueness, and qualitative solution properties of the coupled matrix equations (6.24)-(6.25) that characterize optimal static output feedback when only partial noise-free measurements y(t) = C x(t) are available. Equivalently, solve the underlying optimal static output-feedback problem in a way that clarifies when the coupled equations admit meaningful positive semidefinite solutions.
accepted.context_brief: coupled equations for optimal static output feedback

evidence.quote: Although (6.24) and (6.25) provide a transparent and elegant generalization of (6.8), it is a remarkable fact that virtually nothing is known about their solution properties.
Hence, these two unsolved problems go hand in hand.

accepted.question_text: For the reduced-order linear-quadratic-Gaussian controller problem with controller state dimension n_c < n, analyze the coupled algebraic equations (6.31)-(6.34) and determine when there exist controller matrices A_c, B_c, and C_c such that the closed-loop block matrix [[A, B C_c], [B_c C, A_c]] is asymptotically stable. The source presents the equations and explicitly links their analysis to this unresolved existence problem.
accepted.context_brief: reduced-order LQG algebraic equations and stabilization

evidence.quote: Again a seemingly minor extension of the standard theory has major consequences with respect to the algebraic matrix equations to which it gives rise.

As with the static output-feedback problem, it can also be expected that the analysis of (6.13)-(6.34) is related to the existence of gains A_c, B_c, C_c such that the closed-loop dynamics matrix [A  BC_c; B_c C  A_c] is asymptotically stable.

accepted.question_text: Develop general existence and structural results for the indefinite algebraic Riccati equation A^T P + P A - P Sigma P + gamma^{-2} P V_1 P + R_{1,\infty} = 0 that arises in full-state-feedback H_infinity control. In this equation the quadratic term P (gamma^{-2} V_1 - Sigma) P may be indefinite, and the source notes that, aside from limited prior work, virtually no theory is available for such equations.
accepted.context_brief: indefinite Riccati equations in H-infinity control

evidence.quote: In the full-state-feedback case, enforcement of the constraint ||G(s)||_infinity < gamma leads to ... (6.41).
Now the quadratic term P(gamma^{-2} V_1 - Sigma)P may be indefinite. With the exception of [64], virtually no results on the solutions to such indefinite Riccati equations are available.
